_readme: The only file you edit to add or remove a language. Every content file reads this list, so translations never need to know about each other.
_howToAddALanguage: 1. Copy content.json to content-<code>.json and translate it. 2. Add a line to the array below. That is all - no HTML change, and no edit to the other content files.
_codes: Use a standard language code (en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-br). It becomes the ?lang= value and the <html lang> attribute.
_labels: label is what appears in the toggle. Short is better - EN, ES, FR - since it sits in the nav bar.
_content: content is resolved relative to this file, so a plain filename means the same folder.
_toggleVisibility: The toggle only appears when this array has two or more entries. With one entry the site renders with no language UI at all.
_default: default is the language used when no ?lang= is present. It should match the content file the page points at.
_autoDetect: When true (the default), a first-time visitor whose browser asks for a language you publish gets that language automatically. Set to false to always start on the default and only switch when someone clicks the toggle.
_precedence: ?lang= in the URL wins, then the visitor’s last explicit choice, then the browser language, then default. Clicking the toggle is remembered, so detection never overrides a deliberate choice.
_regionCodes: A browser asking for es-MX or es-419 matches an "es" entry. Publish a region code (pt-br) only if you have a file specifically for it.
_name: name is the language written in itself (English, Espanol, Francais). It appears in the dropdown. label is the short code shown on the badge.
